title: Needle
background: The Thread is the editorial style and visual design magazine of RPI, celebrating fashion and design culture across Troy. The organization needed a digital home for editorial content, event programming, and community contributions—and a secure workspace for officers to manage it all.

Needle is the web-suite built to answer that: public-facing storytelling and internal operations in one platform for viewers, contributors, and authorized members. Developed with a five-person team across design, frontend, and backend.

backgroundImages.alt: The signature mark of The Thread.

process: The Needle web-suite runs on React, Flask, and MongoDB Atlas with AWS S3. API design followed a frontend-first approach, iterating from page-driven routes toward a consolidated events–images–members model.

The Thread anchors every public page as header and footer, setting the design language for the site. Event discovery centers on a card system—several landing layouts, including a Loop component for recent programming, were explored before the team settled on what shipped. Admin breaks deliberately from that aesthetic: The Thread doesn't appear in the workspace, and the visual language shifts sharper and more utilitarian for club officers on the same data.

processImages.alt: Needle data architecture evolution: dataflow draft, schema v2, and proposed entity model
Needle imageDB schema: S3 asset paths, event references, and personnel attribution
Early Figma mockup: The Thread as a winding path with ribbon header navigation and a mixed-scale event card grid
Early landing sketches: Fits of the Week gallery and UPCOMING timeline along The Thread — concepts explored before the shipped event card system
Early Figma mockup: The Loop — a vertical recent-programming stack on the landing hero, explored then cut
Early event card explorations at hero, editorial, and thumbnail scales, with type labels and iconography
Event detail explorations: mobile-first layouts and tablet iconography iterations
Early rounded admin exploration: edit event form with soft corners, type icons, personnel, and image management
Admin portal: Figma exploration vs. shipped login and events management views

result: Needle ships an efficient fullstack dataflow, visually aligned as the digital base of The Thread.
The public interface embodies The Thread’s mission: The Thread itself stitches every page together through soft type and rounded forms—unorthodox and playful, yet systematic.
Published past events—with detailed views, associated images, and members—are live, and the groundwork for a semesterly calendar, member profiles, and PDF publications is laid for future development.

Behind auth, the admin workspace keeps a related but sharper identity: explicitly defined rectangular regions with thin black strokes, resembling a management dashboard yet clearly part of The Thread brand—and a near-complete custom CMS gives officers full data visualization and the infrastructure to manage that same data, with role-based permissions in place.
